voice_instructions: Measured, quiet, a little hushed — calm and unhurried, but with a touch more forward energy than a long documentary; the cold voice of something that read the whole file. Never sensational. Small pauses.

beats.vo: Crete, around nineteen hundred. Arthur Evans's excavations found clay tablets in a script he named Linear A. Today we can sound it out. We still cannot read it.
Its sister script, Linear B, used many of the same signs. In nineteen fifty-two, Michael Ventris deciphered it. It was Greek.
Read with those sound values, Linear A's words can be spoken aloud. But they are not Greek.
They match no language scholars can understand. The Minoan language itself is unknown.
About fourteen hundred inscriptions survive. Decipherments are still claimed. None has been accepted.
